key_insight: Light Coils replace bulky electrical MRI coil cabling with fully optical data transmission, optical power delivery, and optical detuning to enable scalable receive arrays.
engineering_relevance: This architecture can reduce wiring complexity, coupling, and safety constraints while preserving conventional MRI SNR, making ultra-dense modular receiver arrays more practical.
method: Use Mach-Zehnder modulators to map each coil’s MR signal onto a C-band optical carrier.
Power the preamplifiers through power-over-fiber with photovoltaic optical-to-electrical conversion.
Trigger active detuning via an optical control path; extend to multi-channel readout with dense wavelength-division multiplexing on a single fiber.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports matched SNR versus conventional coaxial systems at 5–10 mW MZM input and 80–100 mW photonic power input, plus in vivo 3T brain imaging and four-channel routing with >28 dB inter-channel optical isolation.
watch_item: System performance depends on careful joint optimization of modulator bias, optical power, and front-end gain, which may complicate practical deployment and calibration.
paper_title: Light Coils: MRI with Fully Optical Data and Power Transmission
